title: SQL built by concatenation (vbnet) — review required
description: A vbnet query call assembles SQL from parts: Dim cmd As New SqlCommand("SELECT * FROM users …. If any part is untrusted input, the query structure itself is attacker-controlled. This lexical rule flags the assembly; the reviewer confirms every part is trusted or parameterizes it.
remediation: Parameterize with a SqlParameter bound to @name so input stays data; never interpolate values into SQL text.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any concatenated query matches, including trusted assembly. Input trust needs human review.

tests.line: Dim cmd As New SqlCommand("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" & name & "'", conn)
# audit: Dim cmd As New SqlCommand("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" & name & "'", conn) present
Dim cmd As New SqlCommand("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = @name", conn)
# verified: Dim cmd As New SqlCommand("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = @name", conn)
Dim cmd As New SqlCommand(BuildSql(name) & " -- x", conn)
Dim cmd As New SqlCommand("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = @name", conn)
